text_01: Each record has the paper PDF, the publisher page, and a short summary of the method, evidence and scope.
text_03: Core contribution. A stateful Arbiter-PUF authentication protocol in which each effective challenge depends on the current challenge, a random bit, and the preceding authenticated response, making harvested challenge-response pairs harder to model.
text_05: At 400,000 CRPs, reported prediction accuracy was 51.55% for logistic regression, 52.56% for ANN, and 56.27% for CNN; measured uniformity was 51.57% and uniqueness 49.23%.
text_07: Stateful or machine-learning-resistant PUFs, lightweight IoT authentication, and dependency-chain challenge obfuscation.
text_09: The results are empirical under the evaluated attacks; secure enrollment and correct protocol-state synchronization are assumed, not proven universally.
text_11: Iranian Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering, vol. 21, no. 3, pp. 219–226, 2023
text_12: Core contribution. SQ-PUF uses selected sequence-dependent modules so that the effective challenge depends on prior state and randomness, combining an LFSR with a single Arbiter PUF for lightweight authentication.
text_14: For the principal 400,000-CRP experiment, reported accuracies were 52.14% for logistic regression, 52.40% for ANN, and 50.22% for SVM; uniformity was 50.561% and uniqueness 49.101%.
text_16: Sequence-dependent PUF constructions and lightweight authentication designed to resist evaluated machine-learning attacks.
text_18: The paper is in Persian and reports simulation-based results for specified attack models; secure enrollment and synchronized state remain system assumptions.
text_19: A. Sajadi, N. Zidarič, T. Stefanov, N. Mentens
text_20: Core contribution. After comparing RTL-PAT, PATCH, and ACA, the paper introduces ASSESS: a cycle-accurate VCD plus one-off average-power scan that localizes pre-silicon side-channel leakage without repeatedly storing and processing full time-series traces.
text_22: On a 600-cycle Ibex case, ASSESS completed in 1 h 53 min 9 s versus 72 d 15 h 31 min for ACA, a reported 960× speedup; the corresponding PATCH comparison reports 1,030×.
text_24: Pre-silicon leakage localization, Leakage Impact Factor analysis, gate-level side-channel assessment, or ASSESS runtime improvements.
text_26: Results use GF22FDX gate-level Ibex/Tiny-AES and AES-coprocessor cases; the workflow requires a technology library and power-analysis tooling.
text_27: A. Sajadi, N. Zidarič, T. Stefanov, N. Mentens
text_28: Core contribution. A same-platform security-and-cost comparison of Mask-AES, software and hardware noise generation, Secure-Ibex, and CoCo-Ibex countermeasures for AES software on RISC-V SoCs.
text_30: The baseline key was recovered at about 250 traces; Mask-AES resisted recovery through 21,000 traces at 2.03× code and 1.47× time, while Secure-Ibex resisted 18,000 traces at 1.41×–5.13× time.
text_32: Side-channel security/cost trade-offs, AES on RISC-V, masking, noise generation, secure processors, or compositional countermeasures.
text_34: The study uses first-order CPA on the first AES S-box round on a CW305 Artix-7 platform; results should not be generalized beyond that setup without qualification.
text_36: Core contribution. PROACT integrates resistance to side-channel and fault-injection attacks into the ASIC design flow, using a dual-RISC-V benchmark SoC and pre-silicon analysis to reduce physical-security iteration time.
text_38: The 2024 chapter reports an FPGA prototype approaching tape-out, a simulator-based analysis workflow, and two planned tape-outs.
text_40: Physical-security-by-design, reduced time to market for protected circuits, the PROACT project, or its dual-RISC-V benchmark SoC.
text_42: This is a project-status chapter: planned tape-outs and intended evaluations must not be described as completed results. The local PDF contains only printed pages 255–266.
text_44: Core contribution. A cross-domain snapshot of RISC-V processor testability, safety, and security research, connecting manufacturing and in-field testing with functional safety, cryptographic extensions, side-channel protection, roots of trust, and trusted execution.
text_46: The survey organizes SBST and system-level test, functional and timing safety, cryptographic hardware and ISA extensions, side-channel defenses, and hardware security foundations.
text_48: A broad 2023 overview of dependable and secure RISC-V processors or a taxonomy spanning testability, safety, and security.
text_50: It is a selected research snapshot rather than an exhaustive systematic review; the fast-moving RISC-V ecosystem may have evolved since publication.
text_51: A. Sajadi, N. Zidarič, T. Stefanov, N. Mentens
text_52: Core contribution. A concise CF '26 presentation of the same-platform comparison of AES side-channel countermeasures for RISC-V SoCs, emphasizing the measured security and implementation-cost trade-offs.
text_54: The poster summarizes baseline recovery at about 250 traces, no recovery for Mask-AES through 21,000 traces, and no recovery for Secure-Ibex through 18,000 traces, with their reported overheads.
text_56: The CF '26 poster record or a compact security-versus-cost summary of AES countermeasures on RISC-V SoCs.
text_58: This two-page poster presents the NorCAS experimental study concisely and should not be counted as an independent replication of that work.
